nodes.theorem_title: Reduce the actual P¹ top-degree count by a minimal polynomial
nodes.formal_statement:
theorem AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalP1Minpoly : ∀ (T : Finset AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Qbar),
  AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.IsGalStable T →
    (∀ y ∈ T, ‖AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ι y‖ ≤ 1) →
      ∀ {d n : ℕ},
        2 ≤ d →
          (∀ y ∈ T, AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg y ≤ d) →
            {y ∈ T | AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg y = d}.card ≤ n + 1 →
              ∀ {σ₀ : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Qbar},
                σ₀ ∈ T →
                  AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg σ₀ = d →
                    ∃ (T₂ : Finset AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Qbar) (τ₂ : ℚ),
                      AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.IsGalStable T₂ ∧
                        ↑τ₂ ∉ T₂ ∧
                          (∀ y ∈ T₂, AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg y ≤ d) ∧
                            {y ∈ T₂ | AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg y = d}.card ≤ n ∧
                              ∃ (u : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ElemMap),
                                ∀ (hs : List AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ElemMap),
                                  AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.IsNoncriticalBelyi hs
                                      (AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.withInf T₂)
                                      (AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ofRat τ₂) →
                                    AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.IsNoncriticalBelyi (u :: hs)
                                      (AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.withInf T)
                                      (AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ofRat 9) := by sorry

> Now we perform a “nested induction” on \(m(S),d(S)\): That is to say, we induct on \(m(S)\), and, for each fixed value of \(m(S)\), we induct on \(d(S)\). If \(m(S),d(S)\neq0\), then let \(\alpha_0\in S\backslash\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q})\) be such that \(d_0\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}[\mathbb{Q}(\alpha_0):\mathbb{Q}]\) is equal to \(m(S)+1\). Then by applying an automorphism (with rational coefficients!) as in Lemma 2.3 and then multiplying by some positive rational number, we may assume that \(|\alpha|\leq1\), for all \(\alpha\in S\backslash\{\infty\}\), while \(|\beta|\geq C\), for some sufficiently large \(C\), where “sufficiently large” is relative to \(d_0\). Let \(f_0(x)\in\mathbb{Q}[x]\) be the monic minimal polynomial for \(\alpha_0\) over \(\mathbb{Q}\). Then one verifies immediately that all of the coefficients of \(f_0(x)\) have absolute value \(\leq d_0^{d_0}\). In particular, it follows that the value of \(f_0\) at every \(\alpha\in S\backslash\{\infty\}\), as well as at every element of the set \(S_0\) of roots of the derivative \(f'_0(x)\) has absolute value bounded by some fixed expression in \(d_0\). Thus, for a suitable choice of \(C\), it follows that \(f_0(\beta)\notin S'\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}f_0(S)\cup f_0(S_0)\). Moreover, since \(f_0(\alpha_0)=0\); \([\mathbb{Q}(\alpha'):\mathbb{Q}]<d_0\) for every \(\alpha'\in f_0(S_0)\) [since \(f_0(x),f'_0(x)\in\mathbb{Q}[x]\); \(f'_0(x)\) has degree \(\leq d_0-1\)], it follows that \(S'\) is \(\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})\)-stable and satisfies the property that either \(m(S')<m(S)\) or \(m(S')=m(S);\quad d(S')<d(S)\) — thus completing the induction step. In particular, replacing \(S\) by \(S'\), \(\beta\) by \(f_0(\beta)\), applying the induction hypothesis, and composing the resulting morphisms yields a morphism \(\phi\) as in the statement of Lemma 2.4.

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, Lemma 2.4, complete nested-induction paragraph, printed p. 5.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalP1Minpoly`

Use the full algebraic closure Q̄ of ℚ. A projective point is either ∞ or a finite point some(x), with x ∈ Q̄. The distinguished set is B = {∞, some(0), some(1)}. An elementary map has one of two forms: a rational Möbius map (az+b)/(cz+d), where a,b,c,d ∈ ℚ and ad−bc ≠ 0; or a polynomial p ∈ ℚ[X] with 0 < natDegree(p). At a finite point, a zero Möbius denominator gives ∞. At ∞, a Möbius map gives ∞ when c=0, and some(a/c) otherwise. A polynomial sends some(x) to some(p(x)) and ∞ to ∞. A Möbius map has index 1 at every point. A polynomial has index natDegree(p) at ∞; at some(x), its index is the root multiplicity of x in p mapped to Q̄[X] minus the constant polynomial p(x). For a finite list h = [h₁,…,hₖ], F_h applies h₁ first and hₖ last. Thus F_[] is the identity and F_(u::h)(z)=F_h(u(z)). Its index is R_[]=1 and R_(u::h)(z)=r_u(z)·R_h(u(z)); equivalently, multiply the elementary indices at successive images of z. Write P(h,A,t) for exactly these three conditions: every z ∈ A satisfies F_h(z) ∈ B; F_h(t) ∉ B; and every projective point z with 1 < R_h(z) satisfies F_h(z) ∈ B. For a finite subset T of Q̄, Galois stability means that every ℚ-algebra automorphism σ:Q̄→Q̄ sends every member of T into T. No restriction to a chosen finite extension or rational points occurs. Put D(x)=natDegree(minpoly ℚ x), W(T)={∞}∪{some(x):x∈T}, and q̂=some(q) for q∈ℚ. Fix the ℚ-algebra embedding ι:Q̄→ℂ chosen by IsAlgClosed.lift. Every norm below is the complex norm under this one fixed embedding. Write c_d(T)=#{x∈T:D(x)=d}; this counts distinct elements of the finite set, without multiplicity. Let T be a finite Galois-stable subset of Q̄. Assume ‖ι(y)‖≤1 for every y∈T. Let d,n be natural numbers with 2≤d. Assume D(y)≤d for every y∈T and c_d(T)≤n+1. Choose an element σ₀∈T with D(σ₀)=d. Then there exist a finite subset T₂⊆Q̄ and a rational number τ₂ such that all of the following hold. T₂ is Galois-stable, and the image of τ₂ in Q̄ does not belong to T₂. Every y∈T₂ satisfies D(y)≤d, and c_d(T₂)≤n. There also exists one elementary map u such that, for every finite list hs of elementary maps, P(hs,W(T₂),τ̂₂) implies P(u::hs,W(T),9̂). In u::hs, u acts before hs. This is a continuation contract: it converts any suitable later list for the smaller data into a suitable list for the original data.

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalP1Minpoly`

nodes.theorem_title: Dimension lower bound from the actual function-field basis
nodes.formal_statement:
theorem AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannBasisPowerLowerBound : ∀ {N : ℕ} (M : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Model N) (hDVR : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.PlacesDiscrete M),
  (∀ (A : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Divisor M),
      FiniteDimensional ℚ ↥(AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannRochSpace M hDVR A)) →
    ∀ (l : ℕ),
      (l + 1) * N ≤
        AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannEll M hDVR
          (l • AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.functionPoleDivisor M hDVR M.u +
            AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.basisPoleCorrection M hDVR) := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement:
> “Since $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ is infinite, it thus follows that there exists an $s_1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L})$ such that $s_1(t)\ne0$ for all $t\in T$. Thus, the linear series determined by the sections $s_0,s_1$ of $\mathcal{L}$ has no basepoints, hence determines a finite morphism $\psi:X\to\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$.”

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, proof of Theorem 2.5, printed p. 6.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannBasisPowerLowerBound`

For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. Assume L(A) is finite-dimensional over ℚ for every divisor A. Then for every l∈ℕ, (l+1)N≤ℓ(l(u)∞+C), where C=Σ_i(b_i)∞ is the pole correction of the fixed ℚ(u)-basis b_i=functionBasis M i.

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannBasisPowerLowerBound`

对任意自然数 N 和任意给定模型 M，令 K=M.K 为有理数域与有理函数域 ℚ(X) 的一个固定代数闭包之间的中间域。模型给定 u,v∈K，满足 u 关于有理数域超越、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K 在 ℚ(u) 上有限维且 [K:ℚ(u)]=N。K 的一个处 P 指包含所有有理数的像且真包含于 K 的赋值子环 O_P。记 𝔪_P 为其极大理想，κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P 为其剩余域，剩余映射指商同态 O_P→κ(P)。除子 A 指 K 的全部处上的有限支撑整数值函数；除子不等式指每个处的系数不等式，若每个处 P 都满足 A(P)≥0，则称 A 有效。记 deg(P) 为剩余域 κ(P) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩，deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P)，其中剩余域次数先转为整数。自然数值有限秩在空间有限维时等于通常的向量空间维数。当处 P 的赋值环 O_P 为离散赋值环时，ord_P(f) 表示函数 f 的正规化整数阶，在极大理想的非零元素上为正、在极点处为负，并约定 ord_P(0)=0。等价地 ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f))，其中 v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ 为正规化乘法赋值，ℤᵐ⁰ 是整数加法群改写为乘法记法后再添零元的构造，log 与 exp 是该记法的形式映射，并非实数解析函数。另给定证明 hDVR，断言每个处 P 的赋值环 O_P 都是离散赋值环。对每个除子 A，定义有理数线性子空间 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 或每个处 P 都满足 ord_P(f)≥−A(P)}，并记 ℓ(A) 为 L(A) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩。记 (f)、(f)₀、(f)∞ 分别为逐处系数为 ord_P(f)、max(0,ord_P(f))、max(0,−ord_P(f)) 的有限支撑除子，分别称主除子、零点除子、极点除子。按阶的约定，零函数的这三个除子都等于所有系数均为零的零除子。记 [P] 为在 P 处系数为一且其余系数为零的除子。假设对每个除子 A，L(A) 均在有理数域上有限维。则对每个自然数 l，有 (l+1)N≤ℓ(l(u)∞+C)，其中 C=Σ_i(b_i)∞ 是固定 ℚ(u) 基 b_i=functionBasis M i 的极点修正除子。

**日本語**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannBasisPowerLowerBound`

任意の自然数 N と与えられた任意の模型 M に対し、K=M.K を有理数体と有理関数体 ℚ(X) の固定された代数閉包との間の中間体とする。模型は u,v∈K を与え、u は有理数体上超越的であり、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K は ℚ(u) 上有限次元かつ [K:ℚ(u)]=N を満たす。K の素点 P とは、全ての有理数の像を含み K に真に含まれる付値部分環 O_P をいう。𝔪_P をその極大イデアル、κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P を剰余体とし、剰余写像は商準同型 O_P→κ(P) を表す。因子 A とは K の全ての素点上の有限台を持つ整数値関数である。因子の不等式は各係数の不等式を表し、全ての素点 P で A(P)≥0 なら A を有効という。deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P)、deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P) と書き、剰余体の次数は整数に型変換する。Module.finrank は自然数値の有限階数であり、空間が有限次元なら通常のベクトル空間の次元と一致する。O_P が離散付値環である素点では、ord_P(f) は f の正規化された整数値の位数を表し、極大イデアルの非零元では正、極では負となり、ord_P(0)=0 と定める。同値な表示は ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)) である。v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ は正規化された乗法的付値、ℤᵐ⁰ は整数の加法群を乗法的に書き零元を加えたものであり、log と exp はこの記法の形式的な写像であって実解析の関数ではない。全ての素点 P で O_P が離散付値環であることの任意の証明 hDVR を指定する。各因子 A に対し、有理数線形部分空間 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 または全ての素点 P で ord_P(f)≥−A(P)} を定め、ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A) と書く。(f)、(f)₀、(f)∞ をそれぞれ各素点での係数が ord_P(f)、max(0,ord_P(f))、max(0,−ord_P(f)) となる有限台の因子とし、主因子、零点の因子、極の因子と呼ぶ。位数の規約により、零関数のこれら三つの因子は全ての係数が零である零因子となる。[P] は P での係数が一で他では零である因子を表す。全ての因子 A に対し L(A) が有理数体上有限次元であると仮定する。このとき任意の自然数 l に対し、(l+1)N≤ℓ(l(u)∞+C) である。ここで C=Σ_i(b_i)∞ は固定された ℚ(u) 上の基底 b_i=functionBasis M i の極の補正因子である。

> Proof. Indeed, we induct on the cardinality \(|S|\) of \(S\) and apply Lemma 2.1 [with, say, \(C=2\)] to the set \(\lambda\cdot S\subseteq\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{Q}}\), for some appropriate positive rational number \(\lambda\). Then, so long as \(|S|\geq4\), the polynomial “\(f(x)+f_0\)” of Lemma 2.1 determines a morphism \(\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{Q}}\to\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{Q}}\), unramified away from the image of \(S\), that maps \(\beta,S\) to some \(\beta',S'\) that satisfy conditions (i), (ii), (iii) of the present Lemma 2.2, but for which the cardinalities of \(S',S\) satisfy \(|S'|<|S|\). Thus, by applying the induction hypothesis and composing the resulting morphisms \(\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{Q}}\to\mathbb{P}^1_{\mathbb{Q}}\), we conclude the existence of an “\(f\)”, “\(\phi\)” as in the statement of the present Lemma 2.2.

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, Lemma 2.2, complete proof paragraph, printed p. 4.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalP1Rational`

Use the full algebraic closure Q̄ of ℚ. A projective point is either ∞ or a finite point some(x), with x ∈ Q̄. The distinguished set is B = {∞, some(0), some(1)}. An elementary map has one of two forms: a rational Möbius map (az+b)/(cz+d), where a,b,c,d ∈ ℚ and ad−bc ≠ 0; or a polynomial p ∈ ℚ[X] with 0 < natDegree(p). At a finite point, a zero Möbius denominator gives ∞. At ∞, a Möbius map gives ∞ when c=0, and some(a/c) otherwise. A polynomial sends some(x) to some(p(x)) and ∞ to ∞. A Möbius map has index 1 at every point. A polynomial has index natDegree(p) at ∞; at some(x), its index is the root multiplicity of x in p mapped to Q̄[X] minus the constant polynomial p(x). For a finite list h = [h₁,…,hₖ], F_h applies h₁ first and hₖ last. Thus F_[] is the identity and F_(u::h)(z)=F_h(u(z)). Its index is R_[]=1 and R_(u::h)(z)=r_u(z)·R_h(u(z)); equivalently, multiply the elementary indices at successive images of z. Write P(h,A,t) for exactly these three conditions: every z ∈ A satisfies F_h(z) ∈ B; F_h(t) ∉ B; and every projective point z with 1 < R_h(z) satisfies F_h(z) ∈ B. For a finite subset T of Q̄, Galois stability means that every ℚ-algebra automorphism σ:Q̄→Q̄ sends every member of T into T. No restriction to a chosen finite extension or rational points occurs. Put D(x)=natDegree(minpoly ℚ x), W(T)={∞}∪{some(x):x∈T}, and q̂=some(q) for q∈ℚ. Fix the ℚ-algebra embedding ι:Q̄→ℂ chosen by IsAlgClosed.lift. Every norm below is the complex norm under this one fixed embedding. Write c_d(T)=#{x∈T:D(x)=d}; this counts distinct elements of the finite set, without multiplicity. Let T be a finite subset of Q̄. Assume that every y∈T satisfies ‖ι(y)‖≤1 and D(y)≤1. Then there exists a finite list hs of elementary maps such that P(hs,W(T),9̂). No Galois-stability hypothesis is present. The distinguished rational point is 9, not an arbitrary parameter.

nodes.theorem_title: Principal modification bounded by the actual coordinate pole divisor
nodes.formal_statement:
theorem AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannPolarApproximation : ∀ {N : ℕ} (M : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Model N) (hDVR : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.PlacesDiscrete M)
  (A : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Divisor M),
  ∃ (z : ↥M.K),
    z ≠ 0 ∧
      ∃ (l : ℕ),
        A + AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.functionDivisor M hDVR z ≤
          l • AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.functionPoleDivisor M hDVR M.u := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement:
> “Since $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ is infinite, it thus follows that there exists an $s_1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L})$ such that $s_1(t)\ne0$ for all $t\in T$. Thus, the linear series determined by the sections $s_0,s_1$ of $\mathcal{L}$ has no basepoints, hence determines a finite morphism $\psi:X\to\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$.”

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, proof of Theorem 2.5, printed p. 6.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannPolarApproximation`

For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. For every divisor A, there exist nonzero z∈M.K and l∈ℕ such that A+(z)≤l(u)∞ coefficientwise at every place, where u is the model coordinate.

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannPolarApproximation`

对任意自然数 N 和任意给定模型 M，令 K=M.K 为有理数域与有理函数域 ℚ(X) 的一个固定代数闭包之间的中间域。模型给定 u,v∈K，满足 u 关于有理数域超越、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K 在 ℚ(u) 上有限维且 [K:ℚ(u)]=N。K 的一个处 P 指包含所有有理数的像且真包含于 K 的赋值子环 O_P。记 𝔪_P 为其极大理想，κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P 为其剩余域，剩余映射指商同态 O_P→κ(P)。除子 A 指 K 的全部处上的有限支撑整数值函数；除子不等式指每个处的系数不等式，若每个处 P 都满足 A(P)≥0，则称 A 有效。记 deg(P) 为剩余域 κ(P) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩，deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P)，其中剩余域次数先转为整数。自然数值有限秩在空间有限维时等于通常的向量空间维数。当处 P 的赋值环 O_P 为离散赋值环时，ord_P(f) 表示函数 f 的正规化整数阶，在极大理想的非零元素上为正、在极点处为负，并约定 ord_P(0)=0。等价地 ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f))，其中 v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ 为正规化乘法赋值，ℤᵐ⁰ 是整数加法群改写为乘法记法后再添零元的构造，log 与 exp 是该记法的形式映射，并非实数解析函数。另给定证明 hDVR，断言每个处 P 的赋值环 O_P 都是离散赋值环。对每个除子 A，定义有理数线性子空间 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 或每个处 P 都满足 ord_P(f)≥−A(P)}，并记 ℓ(A) 为 L(A) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩。记 (f)、(f)₀、(f)∞ 分别为逐处系数为 ord_P(f)、max(0,ord_P(f))、max(0,−ord_P(f)) 的有限支撑除子，分别称主除子、零点除子、极点除子。按阶的约定，零函数的这三个除子都等于所有系数均为零的零除子。记 [P] 为在 P 处系数为一且其余系数为零的除子。对每个除子 A，存在非零 z∈M.K 和自然数 l，使每个处的系数都满足 A+(z)≤l(u)∞，其中 u 是模型坐标。

**日本語**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannPolarApproximation`

任意の自然数 N と与えられた任意の模型 M に対し、K=M.K を有理数体と有理関数体 ℚ(X) の固定された代数閉包との間の中間体とする。模型は u,v∈K を与え、u は有理数体上超越的であり、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K は ℚ(u) 上有限次元かつ [K:ℚ(u)]=N を満たす。K の素点 P とは、全ての有理数の像を含み K に真に含まれる付値部分環 O_P をいう。𝔪_P をその極大イデアル、κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P を剰余体とし、剰余写像は商準同型 O_P→κ(P) を表す。因子 A とは K の全ての素点上の有限台を持つ整数値関数である。因子の不等式は各係数の不等式を表し、全ての素点 P で A(P)≥0 なら A を有効という。deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P)、deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P) と書き、剰余体の次数は整数に型変換する。Module.finrank は自然数値の有限階数であり、空間が有限次元なら通常のベクトル空間の次元と一致する。O_P が離散付値環である素点では、ord_P(f) は f の正規化された整数値の位数を表し、極大イデアルの非零元では正、極では負となり、ord_P(0)=0 と定める。同値な表示は ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)) である。v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ は正規化された乗法的付値、ℤᵐ⁰ は整数の加法群を乗法的に書き零元を加えたものであり、log と exp はこの記法の形式的な写像であって実解析の関数ではない。全ての素点 P で O_P が離散付値環であることの任意の証明 hDVR を指定する。各因子 A に対し、有理数線形部分空間 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 または全ての素点 P で ord_P(f)≥−A(P)} を定め、ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A) と書く。(f)、(f)₀、(f)∞ をそれぞれ各素点での係数が ord_P(f)、max(0,ord_P(f))、max(0,−ord_P(f)) となる有限台の因子とし、主因子、零点の因子、極の因子と呼ぶ。位数の規約により、零関数のこれら三つの因子は全ての係数が零である零因子となる。[P] は P での係数が一で他では零である因子を表す。任意の因子 A に対し、非零元 z∈M.K と自然数 l が存在し、全ての素点の係数で A+(z)≤l(u)∞ が成立する。u は模型の座標である。

> “Since $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ is infinite, it thus follows that there exists an $s_1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L})$ such that $s_1(t)\ne0$ for all $t\in T$. Thus, the linear series determined by the sections $s_0,s_1$ of $\mathcal{L}$ has no basepoints, hence determines a finite morphism $\psi:X\to\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$.”

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.exists_ord_pos`

Let K be any field of characteristic zero for which there exists t₀∈K transcendental over ℚ such that K is a finite-dimensional extension of ℚ(t₀). A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. For every f∈K transcendental over ℚ, there exists a place P with ord_P(f)>0.

import Definitions.Def_FermatCurveFieldPlace
import Mathlib.RingTheory.DedekindDomain.Factorization

/-!
# Zeros and poles of functions on a curve

For a curve field `K`:

* every element has only finitely many zeros and poles
  (`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.finite_setOf_ord_ne_zero`,
  `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.finite_setOf_notMem`);
* every nonconstant element (i.e. transcendental over `ℚ`) has a zero and a pole
  (`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.exists_ord_pos`, `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.exists_ord_neg`);
* consequently the elements lying in every place are exactly the constants, i.e. the
  elements algebraic over `ℚ` (`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place.isAlgebraic_iff_forall_mem`).

Both facts are read off the chart ring `A_f`: the zeros of `f` are the height-one primes of
`A_f` containing `f` (finitely many, and at least one since `f` is not a unit of `A_f`).
-/

open IsDedekindDomain

namespace AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K] [IsCurveField K]

/-- A nonconstant function has a zero. -/
theorem exists_ord_pos {f : K} (hf : Transcendental ℚ f) : ∃ P : Place K, 0 < P.ord f := by
  have : Fact (Transcendental ℚ f) := ⟨hf⟩
  have hf0 : f ≠ 0 := ne_zero_of_transcendental hf
  let fB : chartRing f := ⟨f, self_mem_chartRing f⟩
  have hfB0 : fB ≠ 0 := fun h ↦ hf0 (congrArg Subtype.val h)
  have hnu : ¬ IsUnit fB := by
    rintro ⟨u, hu⟩
    apply inv_notMem_chartRing hf
    have h1 : f * ((u⁻¹ : (chartRing f)ˣ) : chartRing f) = 1 := by
      have := congrArg Subtype.val u.mul_inv
      rwa [hu] at this
    rw [← eq_inv_of_mul_eq_one_right h1]
    exact ((u⁻¹ : (chartRing f)ˣ) : chartRing f).2
  obtain ⟨M, hM, hfM⟩ := Ideal.exists_le_maximal (Ideal.span {fB})
    (by rwa [Ne, Ideal.span_singleton_eq_top])
  have hMb : M ≠ ⊥ := by
    intro h
    apply hfB0
    rw [← Ideal.mem_bot, ← h]
    exact hfM (Ideal.mem_span_singleton_self fB)
  let v : HeightOneSpectrum (chartRing f) := ⟨M, hM.isPrime, hMb⟩
  refine ⟨ofChart f v, (ord_pos_iff _).mpr ⟨hf0, ?_⟩⟩
  have hv : fB ∈ ((ofChart f v).toChart f (self_mem_ofChart f v)).asIdeal := by
    rw [toChart_ofChart]
    exact hfM (Ideal.mem_span_singleton_self fB)
  exact (mem_toChart_iff f _ _).mp hv

/-- A nonconstant function has a pole. -/
theorem exists_ord_neg {f : K} (hf : Transcendental ℚ f) : ∃ P : Place K, P.ord f < 0 := by
  obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := exists_ord_pos (transcendental_inv hf)
  exact ⟨P, by rw [ord_inv] at hP; omega⟩

theorem exists_notMem {f : K} (hf : Transcendental ℚ f) : ∃ P : Place K, f ∉ P.1 := by
  obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := exists_ord_neg hf
  exact ⟨P, (ord_neg_iff P).mp hP⟩

variable (K) in
instance : Nonempty (Place K) :=
  let ⟨_, ht⟩ := exists_transcendental K
  let ⟨P, _⟩ := exists_ord_pos ht
  ⟨P⟩

/-- An element lying in every place is a constant (algebraic over `ℚ`). -/
theorem isAlgebraic_of_forall_mem {f : K} (h : ∀ P : Place K, f ∈ P.1) : IsAlgebraic ℚ f := by
  by_contra hf
  obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := exists_notMem hf
  exact hP (h P)

theorem isAlgebraic_iff_forall_mem {f : K} : IsAlgebraic ℚ f ↔ ∀ P : Place K, f ∈ P.1 :=
  ⟨fun hf P ↦ P.mem_of_isAlgebraic hf, isAlgebraic_of_forall_mem⟩

/-- A nonzero element has order `0` everywhere iff it is a constant. -/
theorem isAlgebraic_iff_forall_ord_eq_zero {f : K} :
    IsAlgebraic ℚ f ↔ ∀ P : Place K, P.ord f = 0 := by
  refine ⟨fun hf P ↦ P.ord_eq_zero_of_isAlgebraic hf, fun h ↦ ?_⟩
  by_contra hf
  obtain ⟨P, hP⟩ := exists_ord_pos hf
  exact hP.ne' (h P)

/-- A function has only finitely many zeros. -/
theorem finite_setOf_ord_pos (f : K) : {P : Place K | 0 < P.ord f}.Finite := by
  by_cases hf : IsAlgebraic ℚ f
  · convert Set.finite_empty
    ext P
    simp [P.ord_eq_zero_of_isAlgebraic hf]
  have : Fact (Transcendental ℚ f) := ⟨hf⟩
  have hf0 : f ≠ 0 := ne_zero_of_transcendental hf
  let fB : chartRing f := ⟨f, self_mem_chartRing f⟩
  have hfB0 : fB ≠ 0 := fun h ↦ hf0 (congrArg Subtype.val h)
  have hfin := Ideal.finite_factors (I := Ideal.span {fB}) (by
    rw [Ne, Submodule.zero_eq_bot, Ideal.span_singleton_eq_bot]; exact hfB0)
  refine (hfin.image (ofChart f)).subset ?_
  intro P hP
  have hmem : f ∈ P.1 := P.mem_of_ord_nonneg (le_of_lt hP)
  refine ⟨P.toChart f hmem, ?_, ofChart_toChart f P hmem⟩
  rw [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Ideal.dvd_span_singleton, mem_toChart_iff]
  exact ((P.ord_pos_iff).mp hP).2

/-- A function has only finitely many poles. -/
theorem finite_setOf_ord_neg (f : K) : {P : Place K | P.ord f < 0}.Finite := by
  refine (finite_setOf_ord_pos f⁻¹).subset fun P hP ↦ ?_
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, ord_inv] at hP ⊢
  omega

/-- A function has only finitely many zeros and poles. -/
theorem finite_setOf_ord_ne_zero (f : K) : {P : Place K | P.ord f ≠ 0}.Finite := by
  refine ((finite_setOf_ord_pos f).union (finite_setOf_ord_neg f)).subset fun P hP ↦ ?_
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_union] at hP ⊢
  omega

/-- A function lies in all but finitely many places. -/
theorem finite_setOf_notMem (f : K) : {P : Place K | f ∉ P.1}.Finite :=
  (finite_setOf_ord_neg f).subset fun P hP ↦ (ord_neg_iff P).mpr hP

end AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place

This passage supplies the geometric context of actual divisors, residue-field evaluation and simultaneous nonvanishing. The precise independent Lean constructions and proofs are adapted from Belyi 9ce4d3f793d3bc831f2fc7214b7dbad90ea012d8, pinned by refer/iut, with Apache 2.0 notices retained. nodes.natural_language_statement:
> “Since $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ is infinite, it thus follows that there exists an $s_1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L})$ such that $s_1(t)\ne0$ for all $t\in T$. Thus, the linear series determined by the sections $s_0,s_1$ of $\mathcal{L}$ has no basepoints, hence determines a finite morphism $\psi:X\to\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$.”

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, proof of Theorem 2.5, printed p. 6.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannDefectSup`

For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Define riemannDefectSup M hDVR as the integer supremum of the set {deg(A)−ℓ(A) | A is a divisor}. This definition itself imposes no boundedness or attainment hypothesis.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannEventuallyLinear_of_degree_approximation_basis`

For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). Write (f), (f)₀ and (f)∞ for the finite-support divisors of coefficients ord_P(f), max(0,ord_P(f)) and max(0,−ord_P(f)), respectively; these are the principal divisor, zero divisor and pole divisor of f. By the order convention all three divisors of the zero function are the zero divisor whose coefficients are all zero. Write [P] for the divisor of coefficient one at P and zero elsewhere. Let b_i=functionBasis M i, indexed by Fin(Module.finrank ℚ(u) K), be the fixed chosen ℚ(u)-basis of K. Write B=(u)∞ and C=Σ_i(b_i)∞ for the pole divisor of the model coordinate u and the fixed basis correction. Assume (i) deg((f))=0 for every f∈M.K; (ii) deg(B)=N as an integer; (iii) for every divisor A there exist nonzero z∈M.K and l∈ℕ with A+(z)≤lB coefficientwise; and (iv) for every l∈ℕ, (l+1)N≤ℓ(lB+C). Then there exist integers g₀,N₀ such that every divisor A of degree at least N₀ satisfies ℓ(A)=deg(A)−g₀ over ℤ.

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannDefectSup`

对任意自然数 N 和任意给定模型 M，令 K=M.K 为有理数域与有理函数域 ℚ(X) 的一个固定代数闭包之间的中间域。模型给定 u,v∈K，满足 u 关于有理数域超越、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K 在 ℚ(u) 上有限维且 [K:ℚ(u)]=N。K 的一个处 P 指包含所有有理数的像且真包含于 K 的赋值子环 O_P。记 𝔪_P 为其极大理想，κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P 为其剩余域，剩余映射指商同态 O_P→κ(P)。除子 A 指 K 的全部处上的有限支撑整数值函数；除子不等式指每个处的系数不等式，若每个处 P 都满足 A(P)≥0，则称 A 有效。记 deg(P) 为剩余域 κ(P) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩，deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P)，其中剩余域次数先转为整数。自然数值有限秩在空间有限维时等于通常的向量空间维数。当处 P 的赋值环 O_P 为离散赋值环时，ord_P(f) 表示函数 f 的正规化整数阶，在极大理想的非零元素上为正、在极点处为负，并约定 ord_P(0)=0。等价地 ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f))，其中 v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ 为正规化乘法赋值，ℤᵐ⁰ 是整数加法群改写为乘法记法后再添零元的构造，log 与 exp 是该记法的形式映射，并非实数解析函数。另给定证明 hDVR，断言每个处 P 的赋值环 O_P 都是离散赋值环。对每个除子 A，定义有理数线性子空间 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 或每个处 P 都满足 ord_P(f)≥−A(P)}，并记 ℓ(A) 为 L(A) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩。将 riemannDefectSup M hDVR 定义为整数集合 {deg(A)−ℓ(A) | A 为除子} 的上确界。该定义本身没有有界性或取到上确界的假设。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannEventuallyLinear_of_degree_approximation_basis`

对任意自然数 N 和任意给定模型 M，令 K=M.K 为有理数域与有理函数域 ℚ(X) 的一个固定代数闭包之间的中间域。模型给定 u,v∈K，满足 u 关于有理数域超越、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K 在 ℚ(u) 上有限维且 [K:ℚ(u)]=N。K 的一个处 P 指包含所有有理数的像且真包含于 K 的赋值子环 O_P。记 𝔪_P 为其极大理想，κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P 为其剩余域，剩余映射指商同态 O_P→κ(P)。除子 A 指 K 的全部处上的有限支撑整数值函数；除子不等式指每个处的系数不等式，若每个处 P 都满足 A(P)≥0，则称 A 有效。记 deg(P) 为剩余域 κ(P) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩，deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P)，其中剩余域次数先转为整数。自然数值有限秩在空间有限维时等于通常的向量空间维数。当处 P 的赋值环 O_P 为离散赋值环时，ord_P(f) 表示函数 f 的正规化整数阶，在极大理想的非零元素上为正、在极点处为负，并约定 ord_P(0)=0。等价地 ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f))，其中 v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ 为正规化乘法赋值，ℤᵐ⁰ 是整数加法群改写为乘法记法后再添零元的构造，log 与 exp 是该记法的形式映射，并非实数解析函数。另给定证明 hDVR，断言每个处 P 的赋值环 O_P 都是离散赋值环。对每个除子 A，定义有理数线性子空间 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 或每个处 P 都满足 ord_P(f)≥−A(P)}，并记 ℓ(A) 为 L(A) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩。记 (f)、(f)₀、(f)∞ 分别为逐处系数为 ord_P(f)、max(0,ord_P(f))、max(0,−ord_P(f)) 的有限支撑除子，分别称主除子、零点除子、极点除子。按阶的约定，零函数的这三个除子都等于所有系数均为零的零除子。记 [P] 为在 P 处系数为一且其余系数为零的除子。令 b_i=functionBasis M i 为 K 在 ℚ(u) 上固定选定的基，以 Fin(Module.finrank ℚ(u) K) 为指标。记 B=(u)∞ 为模型坐标 u 的极点除子，C=Σ_i(b_i)∞ 为固定基的极点修正除子。假设：（一）每个 f∈M.K 都满足 deg((f))=0；（二）deg(B)=(N:ℤ)；（三）对每个除子 A，存在非零 z∈M.K 和自然数 l，使逐处系数满足 A+(z)≤lB；（四）对每个自然数 l，有 (l+1)N≤ℓ(lB+C)。则存在整数 g₀,N₀，使每个次数至少为 N₀ 的除子 A 都满足整数等式 ℓ(A)=deg(A)−g₀。

**日本語**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannDefectSup`

任意の自然数 N と与えられた任意の模型 M に対し、K=M.K を有理数体と有理関数体 ℚ(X) の固定された代数閉包との間の中間体とする。模型は u,v∈K を与え、u は有理数体上超越的であり、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K は ℚ(u) 上有限次元かつ [K:ℚ(u)]=N を満たす。K の素点 P とは、全ての有理数の像を含み K に真に含まれる付値部分環 O_P をいう。𝔪_P をその極大イデアル、κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P を剰余体とし、剰余写像は商準同型 O_P→κ(P) を表す。因子 A とは K の全ての素点上の有限台を持つ整数値関数である。因子の不等式は各係数の不等式を表し、全ての素点 P で A(P)≥0 なら A を有効という。deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P)、deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P) と書き、剰余体の次数は整数に型変換する。Module.finrank は自然数値の有限階数であり、空間が有限次元なら通常のベクトル空間の次元と一致する。O_P が離散付値環である素点では、ord_P(f) は f の正規化された整数値の位数を表し、極大イデアルの非零元では正、極では負となり、ord_P(0)=0 と定める。同値な表示は ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)) である。v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ は正規化された乗法的付値、ℤᵐ⁰ は整数の加法群を乗法的に書き零元を加えたものであり、log と exp はこの記法の形式的な写像であって実解析の関数ではない。全ての素点 P で O_P が離散付値環であることの任意の証明 hDVR を指定する。各因子 A に対し、有理数線形部分空間 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 または全ての素点 P で ord_P(f)≥−A(P)} を定め、ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A) と書く。riemannDefectSup M hDVR を整数集合 {deg(A)−ℓ(A) | A は因子} の上限と定める。この定義自体は有界性も上限が達成されることも仮定しない。

Source proof adaptation: Belyi/CurveField/Riemann.lean:158-282 at
9ce4d3f793d3bc831f2fc7214b7dbad90ea012d8.
-/
import Definitions.Def_FermatRiemannLocalDimension
import Mathlib.Data.Int.ConditionallyCompleteOrder

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper

variable {N : ℕ}

/-- The supremum of the actual integer defects. It receives no free genus
or dimension parameter. Boundedness and attainment are proved below. -/
noncomputable def riemannDefectSup (M : Model N) (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M) : ℤ :=
  sSup (Set.range fun A : Divisor M =>
    divisorDegree M A - (riemannEll M hDVR A : ℤ))

/-- The three geometric inputs control actual divisors, actual function
values, and dimensions of actual Riemann–Roch spaces. Their source proof
implies eventual linearity without a separate genus axiom. -/
theorem riemannEventuallyLinear_of_degree_approximation_basis
    (M : Model N) (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M)
    (hDegreeZero : ∀ f : M.K, divisorDegree M (functionDivisor M hDVR f) = 0)
    (hPoleDegree : divisorDegree M (functionPoleDivisor M hDVR M.u) = (N : ℤ))
    (hApprox : ∀ A : Divisor M, ∃ z : M.K, z ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ l : ℕ,
      A + functionDivisor M hDVR z ≤ l • functionPoleDivisor M hDVR M.u)
    (hBasis : ∀ l : ℕ, (l + 1) * N ≤
      riemannEll M hDVR (l • functionPoleDivisor M hDVR M.u +
        basisPoleCorrection M hDVR)) :
    ∃ g0 N0 : ℤ, ∀ A : Divisor M, N0 ≤ divisorDegree M A →
      (riemannEll M hDVR A : ℤ) = divisorDegree M A - g0 := by
  letI : IsCurveField M.K := M.isCurveField
  let B := functionPoleDivisor M hDVR M.u
  let C := basisPoleCorrection M hDVR
  have hC : 0 ≤ C := basisPoleCorrection_nonneg M hDVR
  have hPolarBound : ∃ γ : ℤ, ∀ l : ℕ,
      divisorDegree M (l • B) - (riemannEll M hDVR (l • B) : ℤ) ≤ γ := by
    refine ⟨divisorDegree M C - N, fun l => ?_⟩
    have hcard := hBasis l
    have hdegD : divisorDegree M (l • B + C) = (l : ℤ) * N + divisorDegree M C := by
      rw [divisorDegree_add, divisorDegree_nsmul]
      dsimp only [B]
      rw [hPoleDegree]
    have hmono := RiemannDimension.degreeDefect_mono M hDVR hDegreeZero
      (le_add_of_nonneg_right hC : l • B ≤ l • B + C)
    have hcard' : ((l : ℤ) + 1) * N ≤ riemannEll M hDVR (l • B + C) := by
      exact_mod_cast hcard
    have hexpand : ((l : ℤ) + 1) * N = (l : ℤ) * N + N := by ring
    omega
  obtain ⟨γ, hγ⟩ := hPolarBound
  have hAllBound : ∀ A : Divisor M,
      divisorDegree M A - (riemannEll M hDVR A : ℤ) ≤ γ := by
    intro A
    obtain ⟨z, hz, l, hl⟩ := hApprox A
    have h := RiemannDimension.degreeDefect_mono M hDVR hDegreeZero hl
    rw [divisorDegree_add, hDegreeZero, add_zero,
      RiemannDimension.ell_add_pdiv M hDVR A hz] at h
    exact h.trans (hγ l)
  have hBdd : BddAbove (Set.range fun A : Divisor M =>
      divisorDegree M A - (riemannEll M hDVR A : ℤ)) := by
    exact ⟨γ, by rintro _ ⟨A, rfl⟩; exact hAllBound A⟩
  have hDefectLe : ∀ A : Divisor M,
      divisorDegree M A - (riemannEll M hDVR A : ℤ) ≤ riemannDefectSup M hDVR := by
    intro A
    exact le_csSup hBdd ⟨A, rfl⟩
  obtain ⟨A0, hA0⟩ := Int.csSup_mem (Set.range_nonempty _) hBdd
  change divisorDegree M A0 - (riemannEll M hDVR A0 : ℤ) =
    riemannDefectSup M hDVR at hA0
  refine ⟨riemannDefectSup M hDVR,
    divisorDegree M A0 + riemannDefectSup M hDVR + 1, fun A hA => ?_⟩
  have h1 := hDefectLe (A - A0)
  rw [divisorDegree_sub] at h1
  obtain ⟨z, hz, hle⟩ := RiemannDimension.exists_nonneg_add_pdiv M hDVR hDegreeZero
    (A := A - A0) (by omega)
  have hle' : A0 ≤ A + functionDivisor M hDVR z := by
    intro Q
    have := hle Q
    simp only [Finsupp.coe_add, Finsupp.coe_sub, Pi.add_apply, Pi.sub_apply,
      Finsupp.coe_zero, Pi.zero_apply] at this ⊢
    omega
  have h2 := RiemannDimension.degreeDefect_mono M hDVR hDegreeZero hle'
  rw [divisorDegree_add, hDegreeZero, add_zero,
    RiemannDimension.ell_add_pdiv M hDVR A hz] at h2
  have h3 := hDefectLe A
  omega

end AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper

This passage supplies the geometric context of actual divisors, residue-field evaluation and simultaneous nonvanishing. > “Since $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ is infinite, it thus follows that there exists an $s_1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L})$ such that $s_1(t)\ne0$ for all $t\in T$. Thus, the linear series determined by the sections $s_0,s_1$ of $\mathcal{L}$ has no basepoints, hence determines a finite morphism $\psi:X\to\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$.”

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, proof of Theorem 2.5, printed p. 6.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannRochSpace`

For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). A divisor A is a function from all places of K to ℤ with finite support; inequalities between divisors mean inequalities of every coefficient, and A is effective if A(P)≥0 for every place P. Write deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P) and deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P), with the residue degrees cast to integers. Here Module.finrank is the natural-number-valued finite rank, which is the usual vector-space dimension when finite-dimensionality holds. For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. Supply any proof hDVR that O_P is a discrete valuation ring for every place P of K. For each divisor A define the ℚ-subspace L(A)={f∈K | f=0 or ord_P(f)≥−A(P) for every place P} and ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A). For every divisor A, riemannRochSpace M hDVR A is the ℚ-subspace L(A) defined above. A divisor is an integer-valued function of finite support on all places of M.K.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.mem_riemannRochSpace`

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannRochSpace`

对任意自然数 N 和任意给定模型 M，令 K=M.K 为有理数域与有理函数域 ℚ(X) 的一个固定代数闭包之间的中间域。模型给定 u,v∈K，满足 u 关于有理数域超越、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K 在 ℚ(u) 上有限维且 [K:ℚ(u)]=N。K 的一个处 P 指包含所有有理数的像且真包含于 K 的赋值子环 O_P。记 𝔪_P 为其极大理想，κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P 为其剩余域，剩余映射指商同态 O_P→κ(P)。除子 A 指 K 的全部处上的有限支撑整数值函数；除子不等式指每个处的系数不等式，若每个处 P 都满足 A(P)≥0，则称 A 有效。记 deg(P) 为剩余域 κ(P) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩，deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P)，其中剩余域次数先转为整数。自然数值有限秩在空间有限维时等于通常的向量空间维数。当处 P 的赋值环 O_P 为离散赋值环时，ord_P(f) 表示函数 f 的正规化整数阶，在极大理想的非零元素上为正、在极点处为负，并约定 ord_P(0)=0。等价地 ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f))，其中 v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ 为正规化乘法赋值，ℤᵐ⁰ 是整数加法群改写为乘法记法后再添零元的构造，log 与 exp 是该记法的形式映射，并非实数解析函数。另给定证明 hDVR，断言每个处 P 的赋值环 O_P 都是离散赋值环。对每个除子 A，定义有理数线性子空间 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 或每个处 P 都满足 ord_P(f)≥−A(P)}，并记 ℓ(A) 为 L(A) 在有理数域上的自然数值有限秩。对任意除子 A，riemannRochSpace M hDVR A 定义为上述有理数线性子空间 L(A)。这里除子是 M.K 的全部处上的有限支撑整数值函数。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.riemannRochSpace`

任意の自然数 N と与えられた任意の模型 M に対し、K=M.K を有理数体と有理関数体 ℚ(X) の固定された代数閉包との間の中間体とする。模型は u,v∈K を与え、u は有理数体上超越的であり、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K は ℚ(u) 上有限次元かつ [K:ℚ(u)]=N を満たす。K の素点 P とは、全ての有理数の像を含み K に真に含まれる付値部分環 O_P をいう。𝔪_P をその極大イデアル、κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P を剰余体とし、剰余写像は商準同型 O_P→κ(P) を表す。因子 A とは K の全ての素点上の有限台を持つ整数値関数である。因子の不等式は各係数の不等式を表し、全ての素点 P で A(P)≥0 なら A を有効という。deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P)、deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P) と書き、剰余体の次数は整数に型変換する。Module.finrank は自然数値の有限階数であり、空間が有限次元なら通常のベクトル空間の次元と一致する。O_P が離散付値環である素点では、ord_P(f) は f の正規化された整数値の位数を表し、極大イデアルの非零元では正、極では負となり、ord_P(0)=0 と定める。同値な表示は ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)) である。v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ は正規化された乗法的付値、ℤᵐ⁰ は整数の加法群を乗法的に書き零元を加えたものであり、log と exp はこの記法の形式的な写像であって実解析の関数ではない。全ての素点 P で O_P が離散付値環であることの任意の証明 hDVR を指定する。各因子 A に対し、有理数線形部分空間 L(A)={f∈K | f=0 または全ての素点 P で ord_P(f)≥−A(P)} を定め、ℓ(A)=Module.finrank_ℚ L(A) と書く。任意の因子 A に対し、riemannRochSpace M hDVR A を上記の有理数線形部分空間 L(A) と定める。因子とは M.K の全ての素点上の有限台を持つ整数値関数である。

Authors: The Belyi project contributors

Independent adaptation of the L(A) definition in
Belyi/CurveField/RiemannRochSpace.lean at
9ce4d3f793d3bc831f2fc7214b7dbad90ea012d8.
-/
import Definitions.Def_FermatCurveFieldResidue
import Definitions.Def_FermatCurveFieldZerosPoles
import Definitions.Def_FermatProperDivisorHeight
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Dimension.Finite
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FiniteDimensional.Lemmas

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper

variable {N : ℕ}

/-- The actual Riemann–Roch subspace. The zero element is included
separately because normalized ord has the source's convention ord(0)=0. -/
def riemannRochSpace (M : Model N) (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M)
    (A : Divisor M) : Submodule ℚ M.K := by
  letI : IsCurveField M.K := M.isCurveField
  exact {
    carrier := {f | f = 0 ∨ ∀ P : Place M.K, -A P ≤ ord M hDVR P f}
    zero_mem' := Or.inl rfl
    add_mem' := by
      rintro f g (rfl | hf) (rfl | hg)
      · simp
      · simpa using Or.inr hg
      · simpa using Or.inr hf
      by_cases hfg : f + g = 0
      · exact Or.inl hfg
      refine Or.inr fun P => ?_
      simp only [ord_eq_placeOrd] at hf hg ⊢
      exact (le_min (hf P) (hg P)).trans (P.min_le_ord_add hfg)
    smul_mem' := by
      rintro q f (rfl | hf)
      · simp
      by_cases h : q • f = 0
      · exact Or.inl h
      refine Or.inr fun P => ?_
      rw [Rat.smul_def] at h ⊢
      have hq : (q : M.K) ≠ 0 := left_ne_zero_of_mul h
      have hf0 : f ≠ 0 := right_ne_zero_of_mul h
      rw [ord_eq_placeOrd, P.ord_mul hq hf0, P.ord_ratCast, zero_add]
      simpa only [ord_eq_placeOrd] using hf P }

theorem mem_riemannRochSpace (M : Model N) (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M)
    (A : Divisor M) (f : M.K) :
    f ∈ riemannRochSpace M hDVR A ↔
      f = 0 ∨ ∀ P : Place M.K, -A P ≤ ord M hDVR P f := Iff.rfl

theorem riemannRochSpace_mono (M : Model N) (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M)
    {A B : Divisor M} (h : A ≤ B) :
    riemannRochSpace M hDVR A ≤ riemannRochSpace M hDVR B := by
  rintro f (rfl | hf)
  · exact Or.inl rfl
  exact Or.inr fun P => (neg_le_neg (h P)).trans (hf P)

/-- The actual rational dimension, not a freely specified genus function.
Every theorem that uses finrank as dimension also takes actual finiteness. -/
noncomputable def riemannEll (M : Model N) (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M)
    (A : Divisor M) : ℕ := Module.finrank ℚ (riemannRochSpace M hDVR A)

theorem divisorDegree_add (M : Model N) (A B : Divisor M) :
    divisorDegree M (A + B) = divisorDegree M A + divisorDegree M B :=
  Finsupp.sum_add_index' (fun _ => zero_mul _) (fun _ _ _ => add_mul _ _ _)

@[simp] theorem divisorDegree_zero (M : Model N) :
    divisorDegree M (0 : Divisor M) = 0 := Finsupp.sum_zero_index

noncomputable def divisorDegreeHom (M : Model N) : Divisor M →+ ℤ where
  toFun := divisorDegree M
  map_zero' := divisorDegree_zero M
  map_add' := divisorDegree_add M

theorem divisorDegree_sub (M : Model N) (A B : Divisor M) :
    divisorDegree M (A - B) = divisorDegree M A - divisorDegree M B :=
  map_sub (divisorDegreeHom M) A B

@[simp] theorem divisorDegree_single (M : Model N) (P : Place M.K) (n : ℤ) :
    divisorDegree M (Finsupp.single P n) = n * P.degree :=
  Finsupp.sum_single_index
    (h := fun (Q : Place M.K) (m : ℤ) => m * (Q.degree : ℤ)) (zero_mul _)

theorem divisorDegree_nonneg (M : Model N) {A : Divisor M} (hA : 0 ≤ A) :
    0 ≤ divisorDegree M A :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun P _ => mul_nonneg (hA P) (Int.natCast_nonneg _)

/-- The finite positive part of an actual divisor. -/
noncomputable def divisorPosPart {M : Model N} (A : Divisor M) : Divisor M :=
  Finsupp.mapRange (fun n => max n 0) (by simp) A

theorem divisorPosPart_apply {M : Model N} (A : Divisor M) (P : Place M.K) :
    divisorPosPart A P = max (A P) 0 := Finsupp.mapRange_apply ..

theorem divisorPosPart_nonneg {M : Model N} (A : Divisor M) :
    0 ≤ divisorPosPart A := fun P => by simp [divisorPosPart_apply]

end AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper

This passage supplies the geometric context of actual divisors, residue-field evaluation and simultaneous nonvanishing. The precise independent Lean constructions and proofs are adapted from Belyi 9ce4d3f793d3bc831f2fc7214b7dbad90ea012d8, pinned by refer/iut, with Apache 2.0 notices retained. The paper passage does not state all implementation details. No Belyi, Genl or Iut runtime import is used. > “Since $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ is infinite, it thus follows that there exists an $s_1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L})$ such that $s_1(t)\ne0$ for all $t\in T$. Thus, the linear series determined by the sections $s_0,s_1$ of $\mathcal{L}$ has no basepoints, hence determines a finite morphism $\psi:X\to\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$.”

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, proof of Theorem 2.5, printed p. 6.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.chartRing`

Let K be any field of characteristic zero. For each t∈K, ℚ[t] is the ℚ-subalgebra generated by t, and A_t=chartRing t is its integral closure in K, consisting of elements of K integral over ℚ[t]. For every t∈K, chartRing t is the integral closure in K of the ℚ-subalgebra ℚ[t] generated by t.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.mem_chartRing_of_mem_adjoin`

Let K be any field of characteristic zero. For each t∈K, ℚ[t] is the ℚ-subalgebra generated by t, and A_t=chartRing t is its integral closure in K, consisting of elements of K integral over ℚ[t]. For all t,x∈K, if x∈ℚ[t], then x∈A_t.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.self_mem_chartRing`

Let K be any field of characteristic zero. For each t∈K, ℚ[t] is the ℚ-subalgebra generated by t, and A_t=chartRing t is its integral closure in K, consisting of elements of K integral over ℚ[t]. For every t∈K, t∈A_t.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.ratCast_mem_chartRing`

Let K be any field of characteristic zero. For each t∈K, ℚ[t] is the ℚ-subalgebra generated by t, and A_t=chartRing t is its integral closure in K, consisting of elements of K integral over ℚ[t]. For every t∈K and q∈ℚ, the image of q in K lies in A_t.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.chartRing_le`

Let K be any field of characteristic zero. For each t∈K, ℚ[t] is the ℚ-subalgebra generated by t, and A_t=chartRing t is its integral closure in K, consisting of elements of K integral over ℚ[t]. For every t∈K and subring S⊆K integrally closed in K, if S contains every rational number and t, then A_t⊆S.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.mem_of_mem_chartRing`

Let K be any field of characteristic zero. For each t∈K, ℚ[t] is the ℚ-subalgebra generated by t, and A_t=chartRing t is its integral closure in K, consisting of elements of K integral over ℚ[t]. For every t∈K and valuation subring V⊆K containing ℚ and t, every x∈A_t belongs to V.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.isDedekindDomain_adjoin`

Let K be any field of characteristic zero. For each t∈K, ℚ[t] is the ℚ-subalgebra generated by t, and A_t=chartRing t is its integral closure in K, consisting of elements of K integral over ℚ[t]. For every t∈K transcendental over ℚ, ℚ[t] is a Dedekind domain.

Let K be any field of characteristic zero. For each t∈K, ℚ[t] is the ℚ-subalgebra generated by t, and A_t=chartRing t is its integral closure in K, consisting of elements of K integral over ℚ[t]. For every t∈K supplied as transcendental over ℚ, ℚ[t] is a Dedekind domain.

Let K be any field of characteristic zero for which there exists t₀∈K transcendental over ℚ such that K is a finite-dimensional extension of ℚ(t₀). Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). **简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.chartRing`

设 K 为任意特征零域。对每个 t∈K，ℚ[t] 指由 t 生成的有理数子代数，A_t=chartRing t 是其在 K 中的整闭包，即 K 中在 ℚ[t] 上整的元素组成的环。对任意 t∈K，仿射图环 A_t 定义为由 t 生成的有理数子代数 ℚ[t] 在 K 中的整闭包。

import Definitions.Def_FermatCurveFieldBasic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Polynomial.FieldDivision
import Mathlib.RingTheory.DedekindDomain.IntegralClosure
import Mathlib.RingTheory.DedekindDomain.PID
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Valuation.LocalSubring

/-!
# Affine charts of a curve field

For `t` in a curve field `K` transcendental over `ℚ`, the *chart ring* `A_t` is the integral
closure of `ℚ[t] = Algebra.adjoin ℚ {t}` in `K`. It is the coordinate ring of the affine
open `{t ≠ ∞}` of the regular proper model of the curve: a Dedekind domain, finite over
`ℚ[t]`, of finite type over `ℚ`, with fraction field `K`. Every place of `K` containing `t` is
the localisation of `A_t` at a height-one prime (see `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Place`).

The instances depending on the transcendence of `t` take the hypothesis in the form
`[Fact (Transcendental ℚ t)]`.

## Main definitions and results

* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.chartRing t`: the integral closure of `ℚ[t]` in `K`.
* instances `IsDedekindDomain (chartRing t)`, `IsFractionRing (chartRing t) K`,
  `Module.Finite (Algebra.adjoin ℚ {t}) (chartRing t)`, `Algebra.FiniteType ℚ (chartRing t)`.
* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.chartRing_le`: `A_t` is contained in every integrally closed subring
  containing `ℚ` and `t` (e.g. valuation subrings).
* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.inv_notMem_chartRing`: `t⁻¹ ∉ A_t`, i.e. `t` is not a unit of `A_t`.
-/

open Polynomial
open scoped IntermediateField IntermediateField.algebraAdjoinAdjoin

namespace AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K]

/-- The chart ring `A_t`: the integral closure of `ℚ[t]` in `K`. -/
abbrev chartRing (t : K) : Subalgebra (Algebra.adjoin ℚ {t}) K :=
  integralClosure (Algebra.adjoin ℚ {t}) K

variable {t : K}

theorem mem_chartRing_of_mem_adjoin {x : K} (hx : x ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℚ {t}) :
    x ∈ chartRing t :=
  (chartRing t).algebraMap_mem ⟨x, hx⟩

variable (t) in
theorem self_mem_chartRing : t ∈ chartRing t :=
  mem_chartRing_of_mem_adjoin (Algebra.self_mem_adjoin_singleton ℚ t)

variable (t) in
theorem ratCast_mem_chartRing (q : ℚ) : (q : K) ∈ chartRing t :=
  mem_chartRing_of_mem_adjoin (Subalgebra.algebraMap_mem _ q)

/-- The chart ring is contained in every integrally closed subring containing `ℚ` and `t`. -/
theorem chartRing_le {S : Subring K} [IsIntegrallyClosedIn S K] (hq : ∀ q : ℚ, (q : K) ∈ S)
    (ht : t ∈ S) : (chartRing t).toSubring ≤ S := by
  rw [Subring.integralClosure_le_iff]
  rintro ⟨r, hr⟩
  change r ∈ S
  induction hr using Algebra.adjoin_induction with
  | mem x hx => obtain rfl := Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hx; exact ht
  | algebraMap q => exact hq q
  | add x y _ _ hx hy => exact S.add_mem hx hy
  | mul x y _ _ hx hy => exact S.mul_mem hx hy

/-- The chart ring is contained in every valuation subring containing `ℚ` and `t`. -/
theorem mem_of_mem_chartRing (V : ValuationSubring K) (hq : ∀ q : ℚ, (q : K) ∈ V)
    (ht : t ∈ V) {x : K} (hx : x ∈ chartRing t) : x ∈ V := by
  have : IsIntegrallyClosedIn V.toSubring K := inferInstanceAs (IsIntegrallyClosedIn V K)
  exact chartRing_le (S := V.toSubring) hq ht hx

theorem isDedekindDomain_adjoin (ht : Transcendental ℚ t) :
    IsDedekindDomain (Algebra.adjoin ℚ {t}) := by
  have e := Polynomial.algEquivOfTranscendental ℚ t ht
  have : IsPrincipalIdealRing (Algebra.adjoin ℚ {t}) :=
    IsPrincipalIdealRing.of_surjective e.toRingHom e.surjective
  infer_instance

instance [Fact (Transcendental ℚ t)] : IsDedekindDomain (Algebra.adjoin ℚ {t}) :=
  isDedekindDomain_adjoin Fact.out

/-- The element `t` is not a unit of the chart ring `A_t`. -/
theorem inv_notMem_chartRing (ht : Transcendental ℚ t) : t⁻¹ ∉ chartRing t := by
  have := isDedekindDomain_adjoin ht
  intro h
  have ht0 : t ≠ 0 := ne_zero_of_transcendental ht
  let y : ℚ⟮t⟯ := ⟨t⁻¹, inv_mem (IntermediateField.mem_adjoin_simple_self ℚ t)⟩
  have hy : IsIntegral (Algebra.adjoin ℚ {t}) y := by
    rw [← isIntegral_algHom_iff (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom (Algebra.adjoin ℚ {t}) ℚ⟮t⟯ K)
      (algebraMap ℚ⟮t⟯ K).injective]
    exact h
  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := IsIntegrallyClosed.isIntegral_iff.mp hy
  have hr' : (r : K) = t⁻¹ := congrArg Subtype.val hr
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ : ∃ p : ℚ[X], aeval t p = r := by
    have : (r : K) ∈ (aeval (R := ℚ) t).range := by
      rw [← Algebra.adjoin_singleton_eq_range_aeval]; exact r.2
    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := this

> “Since $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ is infinite, it thus follows that there exists an $s_1\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal{L})$ such that $s_1(t)\ne0$ for all $t\in T$. Thus, the linear series determined by the sections $s_0,s_1$ of $\mathcal{L}$ has no basepoints, hence determines a finite morphism $\psi:X\to\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}$.”

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, proof of Theorem 2.5, printed p. 6.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.transcendental_inv_iff`

Let K be any field of characteristic zero. For every t∈K, t⁻¹ is transcendental over ℚ if and only if t is.

Let K be any field of characteristic zero. For every t∈K transcendental over ℚ, t⁻¹ is also transcendental over ℚ.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.ne_zero_of_transcendental`

Let K be any field of characteristic zero. Every t∈K transcendental over ℚ is nonzero.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.isTranscendenceBasis_of_finiteDimensional`

Let K be any field of characteristic zero for which there exists t₀∈K transcendental over ℚ such that K is a finite-dimensional extension of ℚ(t₀). A place P of K is a valuation subring O_P properly contained in K and containing the image of every rational number. Write 𝔪_P for its maximal ideal, κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P for its residue field, and the residue map for the quotient homomorphism O_P→κ(P). For a place with discrete valuation ring O_P, ord_P(f) denotes the normalized integer order of f, positive on nonzero elements of 𝔪_P and negative on poles; its value at zero is defined to be ord_P(0)=0. Equivalently ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)), where v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ is the normalized multiplicative valuation, ℤᵐ⁰ is the multiplicative copy of ℤ with an added zero, and log and exp are the formal maps for this notation, not real analytic functions. For every natural number N and every given model M, let K=M.K be an intermediate field between ℚ and a fixed algebraic closure of the rational function field ℚ(X). The model supplies u,v∈K such that u is transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, ℚ(u,v)=K, K is finite-dimensional over ℚ(u), and [K:ℚ(u)]=N. `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.exists_finset_adjoin_eq_top`

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.finiteDimensional_adjoin`

K を任意の標数零の体とし、有理数体上超越的な t₀∈K が存在して K は ℚ(t₀) 上有限次元であるとする。K の素点 P とは、全ての有理数の像を含み K に真に含まれる付値部分環 O_P をいう。𝔪_P をその極大イデアル、κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P を剰余体とし、剰余写像は商準同型 O_P→κ(P) を表す。O_P が離散付値環である素点では、ord_P(f) は f の正規化された整数値の位数を表し、極大イデアルの非零元では正、極では負となり、ord_P(0)=0 と定める。同値な表示は ord_P(f)=−log(v_P(f)) である。v_P:K→ℤᵐ⁰ は正規化された乗法的付値、ℤᵐ⁰ は整数の加法群を乗法的に書き零元を加えたものであり、log と exp はこの記法の形式的な写像であって実解析の関数ではない。有理数体上超越的な任意の s∈K に対し、K は ℚ(s) 上有限次元である。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.Model.isCurveField`

任意の自然数 N と与えられた任意の模型 M に対し、K=M.K を有理数体と有理関数体 ℚ(X) の固定された代数閉包との間の中間体とする。模型は u,v∈K を与え、u は有理数体上超越的であり、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K、K は ℚ(u) 上有限次元かつ [K:ℚ(u)]=N を満たす。K の素点 P とは、全ての有理数の像を含み K に真に含まれる付値部分環 O_P をいう。𝔪_P をその極大イデアル、κ(P)=O_P/𝔪_P を剰余体とし、剰余写像は商準同型 O_P→κ(P) を表す。因子 A とは K の全ての素点上の有限台を持つ整数値関数である。因子の不等式は各係数の不等式を表し、全ての素点 P で A(P)≥0 なら A を有効という。deg(P)=Module.finrank_ℚ κ(P)、deg(A)=Σ_P A(P)deg(P) と書き、剰余体の次数は整数に型変換する。Module.finrank は自然数値の有限階数であり、空間が有限次元なら通常のベクトル空間の次元と一致する。体 K は次の条件を満たす。有理数体上超越的な s∈K が存在し、K は ℚ(s) 上有限次元である。

import Definitions.Def_FermatProperCarrier
import Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Rat
import Mathlib.FieldTheory.IntermediateField.Adjoin.Algebra
import Mathlib.FieldTheory.IntermediateField.Adjoin.Basic
import Mathlib.RingTheory.AlgebraicIndependent.AlgebraicClosure
import Mathlib.RingTheory.AlgebraicIndependent.TranscendenceBasis

/-!
# Function fields of curves over number fields

A smooth proper geometrically connected curve over a number field is determined by its
function field. We represent such curves by their function fields: a field `K` of
characteristic `0` which is a finite extension of `ℚ(t)` for some `t ∈ K` transcendental
over `ℚ` (class `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.IsCurveField`). The `ℚ`-algebra structure on `K` is the
canonical one of a field of characteristic zero.

## Main definitions and results

* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.IsCurveField K`: `K` is finite over `ℚ⟮t⟯` for some transcendental `t`.
* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.exists_transcendental`: a curve field has a transcendental element.
* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.trdeg_eq_one`: its transcendence degree over `ℚ` is `1`.
* `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.isAlgebraic_adjoin`, `AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.finiteDimensional_adjoin`:
  for *every* `s ∈ K` transcendental over `ℚ`, `K` is a finite extension of `ℚ⟮s⟯`.
-/

open scoped IntermediateField

namespace AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper

/-- `K` is the function field of a curve over a number field: `K` is finite over `ℚ⟮t⟯` for
some `t ∈ K` transcendental over `ℚ`. -/
class IsCurveField (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] : Prop where
  exists_finite : ∃ t : K, Transcendental ℚ t ∧ FiniteDimensional ℚ⟮t⟯ K

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K]

theorem transcendental_inv_iff {t : K} : Transcendental ℚ t⁻¹ ↔ Transcendental ℚ t :=
  not_congr IsAlgebraic.inv_iff

theorem transcendental_inv {t : K} (ht : Transcendental ℚ t) : Transcendental ℚ t⁻¹ :=
  transcendental_inv_iff.mpr ht

theorem ne_zero_of_transcendental {t : K} (ht : Transcendental ℚ t) : t ≠ 0 := by
  rintro rfl
  exact ht isAlgebraic_zero

/-- If `K` is finite over `ℚ⟮t⟯`, then `{t}` is a transcendence basis of `K / ℚ`. -/
theorem isTranscendenceBasis_of_finiteDimensional {t : K} (ht : Transcendental ℚ t)
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ⟮t⟯ K] : IsTranscendenceBasis ℚ (fun _ : Unit ↦ t) := by
  refine (algebraicIndependent_unique_type_iff.mpr ht).isTranscendenceBasis_iff_isAlgebraic.mpr ?_
  rw [Set.range_const, ← IntermediateField.isAlgebraic_adjoin_iff_top]
  infer_instance

variable [IsCurveField K]

variable (K) in
/-- A curve field contains an element transcendental over `ℚ`. -/
theorem exists_transcendental : ∃ t : K, Transcendental ℚ t :=
  let ⟨t, ht, _⟩ := IsCurveField.exists_finite (K := K); ⟨t, ht⟩

variable (K) in
/-- A curve field has transcendence degree one over `ℚ`. -/
theorem trdeg_eq_one : Algebra.trdeg ℚ K = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht, _⟩ := IsCurveField.exists_finite (K := K)
  have := (isTranscendenceBasis_of_finiteDimensional ht).lift_cardinalMk_eq_trdeg
  simpa using this.symm

/-- Every transcendental element of a curve field is a transcendence basis. -/
theorem isTranscendenceBasis {s : K} (hs : Transcendental ℚ s) :
    IsTranscendenceBasis ℚ (fun _ : Unit ↦ s) :=
  (algebraicIndependent_unique_type_iff.mpr hs).isTranscendenceBasis_of_lift_trdeg_le_of_finite
    (by rw [trdeg_eq_one K]; simp)

/-- A curve field is algebraic over `ℚ⟮s⟯` for every transcendental `s`. -/
theorem isAlgebraic_adjoin {s : K} (hs : Transcendental ℚ s) : Algebra.IsAlgebraic ℚ⟮s⟯ K := by
  have := (isTranscendenceBasis hs).isAlgebraic_field
  rwa [Set.range_const] at this

variable (K) in
/-- A curve field is finitely generated as a field over `ℚ`. -/
theorem exists_finset_adjoin_eq_top :
    ∃ S : Finset K, IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (S : Set K) = ⊤ := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht, _⟩ := IsCurveField.exists_finite (K := K)
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := IntermediateField.fg_top (F := ℚ⟮t⟯) (E := K)
  classical
  refine ⟨insert t S, ?_⟩
  have := congrArg (IntermediateField.restrictScalars ℚ) hS
  have h2 := IntermediateField.adjoin_adjoin_left ℚ (S := {t}) (S : Set K)
  rw [IntermediateField.restrictScalars_top] at this
  rw [Finset.coe_insert, Set.insert_eq, ← h2]
  exact this

/-- A curve field is a finite extension of `ℚ⟮s⟯` for every transcendental `s`. -/
theorem finiteDimensional_adjoin {s : K} (hs : Transcendental ℚ s) :
    FiniteDimensional ℚ⟮s⟯ K := by
  have := isAlgebraic_adjoin hs
  obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := exists_finset_adjoin_eq_top K
  have htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ⟮s⟯ (S : Set K) = ⊤ := by
    rw [← IntermediateField.restrictScalars_eq_top_iff (K := ℚ), eq_top_iff, ← hS,
      IntermediateField.adjoin_le_iff]
    exact IntermediateField.subset_adjoin _ _
  have := IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_adjoin (K := ℚ⟮s⟯) (S := (S : Set K))
    (fun x _ ↦ (Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isAlgebraic x).isIntegral)
  rw [htop] at this
  exact IntermediateField.topEquiv.toLinearEquiv.finiteDimensional


/-- The source class has one field, already present in the fixed model. -/
theorem Model.isCurveField {N : ℕ} (M : Model N) : IsCurveField M.K :=
  ⟨⟨M.u, M.transcendental_u, M.finite_u⟩⟩

end AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper

This passage supplies the geometric context of actual divisors, residue-field evaluation and simultaneous nonvanishing. The precise independent Lean constructions and proofs are adapted from Belyi 9ce4d3f793d3bc831f2fc7214b7dbad90ea012d8, pinned by refer/iut, with Apache 2.0 notices retained. The paper passage does not state all implementation details. No Belyi, Genl or Iut runtime import is used. Belyi/CurveField/Basic.lean:40–136; the exact one-field curve-function-field class is witnessed by the existing Model.u, transcendental_u and finite_u. No constant-field equality or finite-type-field premise is added.

theorem AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalP1Normalize : ∀ (T : Finset AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Qbar),
  AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.IsGalStable T →
    ∀ {τ : ℚ},
      ↑τ ∉ T →
        ∃ (u : AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ElemMap) (T₁ : Finset AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Qbar),
          AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.IsGalStable T₁ ∧
            (∀ y ∈ T₁, ‖AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ι y‖ ≤ 1) ∧
              (∀ (d : ℕ),
                  1 ≤ d →
                    (∀ t ∈ T, AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg t ≤ d) →
                      (∀ y ∈ T₁, AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg y ≤ d) ∧
                        (2 ≤ d →
                          {y ∈ T₁ | AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg y = d}.card ≤
                            {t ∈ T | AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg t = d}.card)) ∧
                ∀ (hs : List AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ElemMap),
                  AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.IsNoncriticalBelyi hs
                      (AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.withInf T₁)
                      (AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ofRat 9) →
                    AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.IsNoncriticalBelyi (u :: hs)
                      (AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.withInf T)
                      (AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ofRat τ) := by sorry
nodes.natural_language_statement:
> Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})\) be a finite set of complex points. Then for any real \(C>0\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb{C}\backslash S\subseteq\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})\backslash S\), there exists a \(\lambda\in\mathbb{C}\) such that the rational function \(f(x)=1/(x-\lambda)\) satisfies \(f(\beta)\neq0,\infty\); \(f(\alpha)\neq\infty\); and \(|f(\beta)|\geq C\cdot|f(\alpha)|\), for all \(\alpha\in S\). Moreover, if \(\beta\in\mathbb{Q}\), then one may take \(\lambda\in\mathbb{Q}\).

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, Lemma 2.3, complete statement paragraph, printed p. 4.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalP1Normalize`

Use the full algebraic closure Q̄ of ℚ. A projective point is either ∞ or a finite point some(x), with x ∈ Q̄. The distinguished set is B = {∞, some(0), some(1)}. An elementary map has one of two forms: a rational Möbius map (az+b)/(cz+d), where a,b,c,d ∈ ℚ and ad−bc ≠ 0; or a polynomial p ∈ ℚ[X] with 0 < natDegree(p). At a finite point, a zero Möbius denominator gives ∞. At ∞, a Möbius map gives ∞ when c=0, and some(a/c) otherwise. A polynomial sends some(x) to some(p(x)) and ∞ to ∞. A Möbius map has index 1 at every point. A polynomial has index natDegree(p) at ∞; at some(x), its index is the root multiplicity of x in p mapped to Q̄[X] minus the constant polynomial p(x). For a finite list h = [h₁,…,hₖ], F_h applies h₁ first and hₖ last. Thus F_[] is the identity and F_(u::h)(z)=F_h(u(z)). Its index is R_[]=1 and R_(u::h)(z)=r_u(z)·R_h(u(z)); equivalently, multiply the elementary indices at successive images of z. Write P(h,A,t) for exactly these three conditions: every z ∈ A satisfies F_h(z) ∈ B; F_h(t) ∉ B; and every projective point z with 1 < R_h(z) satisfies F_h(z) ∈ B. For a finite subset T of Q̄, Galois stability means that every ℚ-algebra automorphism σ:Q̄→Q̄ sends every member of T into T. No restriction to a chosen finite extension or rational points occurs. Put D(x)=natDegree(minpoly ℚ x), W(T)={∞}∪{some(x):x∈T}, and q̂=some(q) for q∈ℚ. Fix the ℚ-algebra embedding ι:Q̄→ℂ chosen by IsAlgClosed.lift. Every norm below is the complex norm under this one fixed embedding. Write c_d(T)=#{x∈T:D(x)=d}; this counts distinct elements of the finite set, without multiplicity. Let T be a finite Galois-stable subset of Q̄. Let τ be any rational number whose image in Q̄ is not in T. Then there exist one elementary map u and one finite subset T₁⊆Q̄ with the following properties. T₁ is Galois-stable, and every y∈T₁ satisfies ‖ι(y)‖≤1. For every natural number d with 1≤d, if D(t)≤d for every t∈T, then D(y)≤d for every y∈T₁. Under those same assumptions on d and T, if also 2≤d, then c_d(T₁)≤c_d(T). Finally, for every finite list hs of elementary maps, P(hs,W(T₁),9̂) implies P(u::hs,W(T),τ̂). In u::hs, u acts first. The same u and T₁ serve all d and all continuation lists hs.

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalP1Normalize`

nodes.natural_language_statement:
> Theorem 2.5. (Belyi Maps Noncritical at Prescribed Points) Let X be a smooth, proper, connected curve over \overline{\mathbb{Q}} and S,T \subseteq X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) finite sets of \overline{\mathbb{Q}}-rational points such that S \cap T = \emptyset. Then there exists a morphism \phi : X \to \mathbb{P}^{1}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}} such that: (a) \phi is unramified over \mathbb{P}^{1}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\backslash\{0,1,\infty\}; (b) \phi(S) \subseteq \{0,1,\infty\}; (c) we have \phi(T) \cap \{0,1,\infty\} = \emptyset. Moreover, if X, S, and T are defined over a number field F, then \phi may be taken to be defined over F.

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, Theorem 2.5, printed pp. 5–6.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalDerivativeBadPlacesFinite`

Let N be any natural number and M a given Model(N). This does not assert that such a model exists for every N. Its field K=M.K is an intermediate field over ℚ in an algebraic closure of ℚ(X). It has specified elements u,v with u transcendental over ℚ, u^N+v^N=1, and ℚ(u,v)=K. The extension K/ℚ(u) is finite-dimensional with dimension N. A place P of K is an actual valuation subring O_P⊊K containing every rational number. The carrier includes every such subring; it selects no affine chart. Membership f∈O_P is the source meaning of f being regular at P. A pole here means f∉O_P. The derivative D_ψ is the actual function CurveDeriv.derivAlong(ψ), not an arbitrary supplied derivation. For a characteristic-zero field K and ψ∈K, this function tests whether ψ is transcendental over ℚ and K is algebraic over ℚ(ψ). If both hold, it takes the formal polynomial derivative on ℚ[ψ] and extends it to K through the canonical Kähler differential equivalence for the formally étale extension ℚ[ψ]→K. If the conjunction fails, D_ψ is the zero derivation. Let ψ∈K be transcendental over ℚ. Then the set of all places P of K for which both following conditions hold is finite. First, ψ∈O_P. Second, there exists s∈K with s∈O_P and D_ψ(s)∉O_P. Equivalently, among all places where ψ is regular, only finitely many local rings fail to be preserved by this actual derivation. The conclusion is finiteness of places, not finiteness of possible witnesses s. The theorem has no discrete-valuation, residue-field-finiteness, or ramification hypothesis. This source theorem is open: its body is by sorry.

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalDerivativeBadPlacesFinite`

设 N 为任意自然数，M 为给定的 Model(N)。这里不声称每个 N 都存在这样的模型。其域 K=M.K 是有理函数域 ℚ(X) 的某个代数闭包中包含有理数域的中间域。模型指定元素 u,v，满足 u 在有理数域上超越、u^N+v^N=1、ℚ(u,v)=K；扩张 K/ℚ(u) 有限维且维数为 N。K 的一个处 P 是实际的赋值子环 O_P，满足 O_P≠K，并包含全部有理数。处的类型遍历所有这样的子环，不选择仿射图。f∈O_P 就是源代码中 f 在 P 处正则的含义；这里的极点指 f∉O_P。导子 D_ψ 是实际定义的函数 CurveDeriv.derivAlong(ψ)，不是任意另给的导子。对特征为零的域 K 及 ψ∈K，该定义检验两个条件：ψ 在有理数域上超越，且 K 在 ℚ(ψ) 上为代数扩张。两个条件都成立时，取 ℚ[ψ] 上的形式多项式求导，并通过形式平展扩张 ℚ[ψ]→K 的标准 Kähler 微分等价将其延拓到 K。若该合取不成立，则 D_ψ 是零导子。设 ψ∈K 在有理数域上超越。则满足以下两个条件的 K 的全部处 P 所成的集合是有限集：第一，ψ∈O_P；第二，存在 s∈K，使 s∈O_P 且 D_ψ(s)∉O_P。也就是说，在 ψ 正则的全部处中，只有有限多个处的局部环不被这个实际导子保持。结论是处集合有限，不是可能的见证元素 s 只有有限多个。该定理没有离散赋值、剩余域有限维或分歧方面的假设。该源定理尚未证明，证明体为 by sorry。

**日本語**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.noncriticalDerivativeBadPlacesFinite`

N を任意の自然数、M を与えられた Model(N) とする。これは各 N に対するモデルの存在を主張しない。その体 K=M.K は、有理関数体 ℚ(X) のある代数閉包内の ℚ 上の中間体である。指定された元 u,v は、u が ℚ 上超越的であること、u^N+v^N=1、および ℚ(u,v)=K を満たす。また K/ℚ(u) は有限次元であり、その次元は N である。K の場所 P は、すべての有理数を含む真の付値部分環 O_P⊊K そのものである。場所の型はこのような部分環すべてを含み、アフィン座標近傍を選ばない。f∈O_P が、このソースで f が P で正則であるという意味であり、ここで極とは f∉O_P をいう。導分 D_ψ は実際に定義された関数 CurveDeriv.derivAlong(ψ) であり、任意に与えた導分ではない。標数零の体 K と ψ∈K に対して、この定義は、ψ が ℚ 上超越的であり、かつ K が ℚ(ψ) 上代数的であるかを調べる。両条件が成り立つ場合、ℚ[ψ] 上の形式的な多項式微分を、形式的エタール拡大 ℚ[ψ]→K に対する標準的なケーラー微分の同値を通じて K に延長する。この連言が偽ならば D_ψ は零導分である。ψ∈K が ℚ 上超越的であるとする。このとき、次の二条件をともに満たす K のすべての場所 P の集合は有限である。第一に ψ∈O_P である。第二に、s∈O_P かつ D_ψ(s)∉O_P を満たす元 s∈K が存在する。すなわち、ψ が正則であるすべての場所のうち、この実際の導分が局所環を保たない場所は有限個である。結論は場所の集合の有限性であり、証人となる元 s の候補の有限性ではない。この定理には、離散付値性、剰余体の有限次元性、分岐についての仮定はない。このソースの定理は未証明であり、証明本体は by sorry である。

nodes.natural_language_statement:
> Thus, in summary, by replacing \(X\) by \(\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\), \(T\) by the point “0” of \(\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\), and \(S\) by the union of \(\psi(S)\) and the points of \(\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\) over which \(\psi\) ramifies, we conclude that we may reduce to the case \(X=\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\), \(T=\{\beta\}\), for some \(\beta\in\mathbb{P}^1(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})\backslash\{\infty\}\). Next, by applying Lemma 2.4, one reduces to the case \(X=\mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}}\), \(S\subseteq\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q})\), \(T=\{\beta\}\), for some \(\beta\in\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{Q})\backslash\{\infty\}\). Finally, by applying an automorphism as in Lemma 2.3 [for, say, \(C=4\)], followed by a suitable automorphism of the form \(x\mapsto\nu\cdot x+\mu\), where \(\nu\in\{\pm1\}\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb{Q}\), gives rise to a situation in which the hypotheses of Lemma 2.2 are valid. Thus, Theorem 2.5 follows from Lemma 2.2.

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Noncritical Belyi Maps*, Theorem 2.5, final proof paragraph (begins at bottom of p.6 and ends at top of p.7), printed p. 6, 7.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ofRat`

For each rational number q, define ofRat(q) to be the finite projective point some(q), using the canonical inclusion ℚ→Q̄. The projective point type is Option Q̄; none represents ∞.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.IsGalStable`

For a finite subset T of the full algebraic closure Q̄ of ℚ, define IsGalStable(T) as follows. For every ℚ-algebra automorphism σ:Q̄≃Q̄, and every t∈T, one has σ(t)∈T.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.deg`

For each element x of the full algebraic closure Q̄ of ℚ, define deg(x) as the natural-number degree of its minimal polynomial over ℚ.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.withInf`

For a finite subset T of Q̄, define withInf(T) as the set {∞}∪{some(t):t∈T} of projective points. Here a projective point has type Option Q̄, and none represents ∞.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.none_mem_withInf`

For every finite subset T of Q̄, the point ∞ belongs to withInf(T)={∞}∪{some(t):t∈T}. Here ∞ is none in Option Q̄.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.some_mem_withInf`

For every finite subset T of Q̄ and every t∈Q̄, if t∈T, then the finite projective point some(t) belongs to withInf(T)={∞}∪{some(x):x∈T}.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ι`

Define ι to be one fixed ℚ-algebra homomorphism from the full algebraic closure Q̄ of ℚ into ℂ. The definition supplies the local instance that Q̄ is algebraic over ℚ, then uses IsAlgClosed.lift. As a field homomorphism, ι is an embedding.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.ι_ratCast`

For every rational number q, the fixed ℚ-algebra embedding ι:Q̄→ℂ sends the canonical image of q in Q̄ to its canonical image in ℂ: ι((q:Q̄))=(q:ℂ).

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.norm_ι_ratCast`

For every rational number q, the complex norm of its image under the fixed ℚ-algebra embedding ι:Q̄→ℂ equals the real absolute value of q: ‖ι((q:Q̄))‖=|(q:ℝ)|.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.IsNoncriticalBelyi`

Use the full algebraic closure Q̄ of ℚ. A projective point is either ∞ or a finite point some(x), with x ∈ Q̄. The distinguished set is B = {∞, some(0), some(1)}. An elementary map has one of two forms: a rational Möbius map (az+b)/(cz+d), where a,b,c,d ∈ ℚ and ad−bc ≠ 0; or a polynomial p ∈ ℚ[X] with 0 < natDegree(p). At a finite point, a zero Möbius denominator gives ∞. At ∞, a Möbius map gives ∞ when c=0, and some(a/c) otherwise. A polynomial sends some(x) to some(p(x)) and ∞ to ∞. A Möbius map has index 1 at every point. A polynomial has index natDegree(p) at ∞; at some(x), its index is the root multiplicity of x in p mapped to Q̄[X] minus the constant polynomial p(x). For a finite list h = [h₁,…,hₖ], F_h applies h₁ first and hₖ last. Thus F_[] is the identity and F_(u::h)(z)=F_h(u(z)). Its index is R_[]=1 and R_(u::h)(z)=r_u(z)·R_h(u(z)); equivalently, multiply the elementary indices at successive images of z. Write P(h,A,t) for exactly these three conditions: every z ∈ A satisfies F_h(z) ∈ B; F_h(t) ∉ B; and every projective point z with 1 < R_h(z) satisfies F_h(z) ∈ B. For every finite list hs of these elementary maps, every set S of projective points, and every projective point τ, define IsNoncriticalBelyi(hs,S,τ) to mean P(hs,S,τ). The definition is exactly the conjunction above.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.NoncriticalP1.IsNoncriticalBelyi.mono`

Use the full algebraic closure Q̄ of ℚ. A projective point is either ∞ or a finite point some(x), with x ∈ Q̄. The distinguished set is B = {∞, some(0), some(1)}.
